name: What inspections happen during detached ADU construction?

mainEntity.name: What inspections are usually required during detached ADU construction in Los Angeles, and in what order do they happen?
mainEntity.text: What inspections are usually required during detached ADU construction in Los Angeles, and in what order do they happen?

acceptedAnswer.text: Detached ADU construction usually moves through a standard inspection sequence, and missing one step can stall the whole project. The exact order varies by jurisdiction and project type, but the common checkpoints are foundation or footing, framing, rough plumbing, rough electrical, rough mechanical, insulation, drywall, and final inspection. Some projects also require special inspections for grading, soil conditions, or structural elements. Homeowners should ask the builder for an inspection calendar before work begins so that trades are not buried before approval. This is especially important for fast-moving projects, where one missed inspection can delay the next phase. The best contractors plan the schedule around inspection availability rather than trying to inspect after the fact. A clean inspection record is one of the strongest signs that the project is moving properly and that the permit set was prepared well.
